task.title: Let readers choose the version they read
task.shortdesc: The version picker beside the site title decides which version of the docs readers are served: their own, one fixed version, one they choose from a list you set, or no picker at all.

context.p: Each reader normally gets the version their organization is entitled to, and anonymous visitors of a public site get the version of the public set. The version picker belongs to the registered repository and is kept in the database, like the access mode, so only an operator can change it. New repositories have it off.

strow.stentry: The release label, as without a picker
The one the reader chose; at first, their own
A menu of the listed versions and the reader's own, newest first

step.cmd: Choose a mode on the Site & access page of the admin console, under Version picker, or through the admin API.

stepxmp.codeblock: H="authorization: Bearer $OPEND_ADMIN_TOKEN" curl -X PUT "$PUBLIC_URL/admin/api/repos/1/versions" -H "$H" -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"mode":"list","versions":["2.1","2.0","1.4"]}' # or {"mode":"fixed","version":"2.1"}, {"mode":"reader"}, {"mode":"off"}

stepresult.p: Every replica drops its cached pages at once, so the next page shows the new picker.

step.cmd: Or set it in a seed file, next to the repository.

stepxmp.codeblock: repos: - fullName: acme/docs sourceUrl: https://github.com/acme/docs.git versionPicker: { mode: list, versions: ['2.1', '2.0', '1.4'] }

info.p: A seed without versionPicker leaves the picker as it is.

ul.li: Only the version changes. Products and features still come from the reader's entitlements (and the public set on a public site), so a reader who switches to 2.0 sees 2.0's content for the products they hold. Release conditions and the release line follow the version served.

Listing a version opens it. Every reader may switch to any listed version, whatever their own. On a public site that includes anonymous visitors: with no public set, they then see content gated only by release, never by product or feature. A fixed version is served to everyone in the same way.

A choice is only a request. It is kept in the opend_version cookie by the picker's links (/_version?v=2.0&returnTo=/page.html) and checked on every request: a version the picker no longer offers is ignored, and the reader is back on their own.

Everything follows it. Pages, navigation, search, images and PDFs are served for the version chosen, and cached per version. The staff view moves to the chosen version's release line. The embedded help panel and the public API are unchanged: they always use the reader's own version.
The picker is a list of links in a <details> menu, so it works without scripts, and sits in the Menu panel on narrow screens. See .
